title: Multiprecision computation of bright and dark solitons in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara, Farrell T. Adriano, Hadi Susanto
abstract: We study the spectral stability of bright and dark solitons in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation using multiprecision arithmetic. The eigenvalues governing stability are exponentially small in the lattice spacing and cannot be resolved with standard double precision. To address this, we develop a computational framework combining multiprecision arithmetic, an exact Jacobian for the stationary problem, and a squared-operator formulation for spectral analysis. This enables accurate resolution of exponentially small eigenvalues and direct comparison with exponential-asymptotic predictions. Our results show that onsite bright solitons are spectrally stable, whereas intersite bright solitons and both onsite and intersite dark solitons are unstable. Bright solitons require only a few eigenvalues and allow efficient large-scale computations, while dark solitons demand higher precision due to their proximity to the continuous spectrum. Simulations up to \(N=65{,}250\) grid points (31.7 GB RAM) highlight the necessity of multiprecision arithmetic for capturing beyond-all-orders spectral effects.
summary: This work develops a high-precision computational framework to analyze the spectral stability of solitons in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation. By employing multiprecision arithmetic, the authors accurately resolve exponentially small eigenvalues, determining that onsite bright solitons are stable while other configurations are unstable. This highlights the computational challenges in studying nonlinear wave dynamics near continuum limits.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spectral stability of bright and dark solitons governed by the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation.
main_result: Onsite bright solitons are found to be spectrally stable, while intersite bright and all dark solitons are unstable. The study demonstrates the necessity of multiprecision arithmetic to resolve exponentially small eigenvalues.
method: A computational framework combining multiprecision arithmetic, an exact Jacobian for the stationary problem, and a squared-operator formulation is developed for spectral analysis.
model_or_system: The primary model is the one-dimensional DNLS equation, which describes nonlinear wave phenomena in discrete lattices. The continuous limit ($h 	o 0$) corresponds to the standard NLS equation.
key_observables: Spectral eigenvalues ($\lambda$) determining stability, and the profiles of onsite/intersite bright and dark solitons.
important_parameters: Lattice spacing ($h$), nonlinearity parameter ($\sigma$), and the required working precision (MP).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that standard double precision fails to resolve the stability eigenvalues, necessitating high-precision computation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the profiles and spectra for bright solitons (onsite/intersite) and dark solitons, confirming asymptotic predictions for bright solitons.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the DNLS model and the standing wave ansatz. It then details the numerical methods, emphasizing the use of multiprecision arithmetic to solve the nonlinear system and compute the spectrum via the squared-operator formulation.
why_interesting: The rigorous computational techniques developed for handling exponentially small eigenvalues in nonlinear lattice systems are highly relevant for analyzing stability in quantum optics and many-body systems where continuum limits are approached.
